title: Project Overview
description: Start with the README, which covers Windows installation, first run with Zalo, the desktop app and the admin UI. PROJECT_MAP.md adds a navigation map of the architecture, so together they frame the bot before you open any code.

title: Entry Points and CLI
description: pyproject.toml declares the package and its optional extras, and the CLI entry bot.cli:main resolves to command_line.py. That file has a fan-out of 9 and is the argparse front door: run, console, webhook management, gateway/admin control. __main__.py and the PyInstaller zalobot_entry.py both delegate to it, so every launch path converges here.
languageLesson: Python console scripts: the [project.scripts] table in pyproject.toml maps a command name to a module:function, and python -m package runs __main__.py.

title: Configuration and Paths
description: config.py (fan-in 18) holds the typed Settings dataclass loaded from the environment or .env with validation. userdata_paths.py (fan-in 13) resolves where userdata lives, for a frozen exe versus source. Nearly everything later depends on these two, so learn them first.

title: Persistence Layer
description: The storage package is a barrel that re-exports file-backed stores. text_files.py supplies atomic writes and JSON-lines wrappers, and data_stores.py builds group settings, chat history and memory on top of them. vietnam_time.py (fan-in 14) is the shared fixed UTC+7 time helper these stores use.

title: Receiving Zalo Messages
description: The zalo package normalizes incoming messages into the IncomingMessage dataclass. They arrive via long polling, an authenticated FastAPI webhook, or a personal account through the unofficial zlapi library. The Bot Platform client handles outgoing calls.

title: The Message Orchestrator
description: message_handler.py (fan-out 12) is the central Bot class. It owns the stores, filter, commands and rate limiters, and queues work per chat. It builds on the stores from Step 4 and the incoming messages from Step 5.

title: Roles and Commands
description: roles.py defines the basic/leader/owner hierarchy and the minimum role each command needs. owner_commands.py parses slash commands and enforces those roles. docs/lenh-zalo.md documents the same commands for end users.

title: Gemini Agent
description: Messages that pass the filter reach GeminiAgent, which runs a bounded function-calling loop with retries. The system prompt is built from hot-reloaded SYSTEM.md and MEMORY.md, and ToolRegistry discovers tool modules. Reply formatting then prepares the answer for Zalo's length limits.

title: Agent Tools
description: Tools give the model abilities such as scheduling events, assigning calendar items and reading chat memory. A template (_example.py) shows how to declare a new tool, and users can drop in their own.

title: Process and System Operations
description: bot_process.py controls the bot lifecycle: PID files, locks, spawn, stop and restart. Around it sit auto_update, handover between local and VPS, remote config sync and the remote server client. Together they let one codebase run on a desktop or a server.

title: Admin Web UI
description: admin_web_server.py has the highest fan-out in the project (21). This FastAPI factory wires auth, bot control, handover, groups and history. The static index.html and admin_page.js form a single-page front end served from it, and settings_file.py edits .env safely.

title: Desktop App
description: desktop_app.py hosts the admin server inside a native window and controls the bot, with a pystray tray menu and a Windows autostart entry. It is the user-facing shell over the admin UI from Step 11.

title: Packaging and Deployment
description: ZaloBot.cmd bootstraps a virtualenv, and build-exe.ps1 with the PyInstaller spec produces a single-file ZaloBot.exe. check_secrets.py audits the build for leaked files. Task Scheduler and supervisor scripts keep it running, and docs/vps-dieu-khien.md explains VPS control.

title: Test Suite
description: conftest.py provides fake Zalo and Gemini fixtures used by many tests. test_bot.py and test_roles.py cover the orchestrator and role rules, and test_admin.py and test_handover.py cover the admin API and data transfer.
